subject: Re: RetailCo discovery — model fit & regression concern
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@retailco.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: RetailCo discovery — model fit & next steps

Hi Sarah —

Great speaking with you today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery:

- Primary goal: reduce false positives in product categorization for web catalog ingestion; target precision improvement of +8–10%.
- Current infra: RetailCo ingests ~1.2M items/day; typical prompt length ~120 tokens; peak latency requirement <400ms for interactive review UI.
- Sensitive data: PII stripped upstream; still need SOC2 evidence and audit-log retention (we discussed Dedicated/Private options).

Model fit recommendations (initial):
- redwood-rlm-1.1 (recommended): strong on short-form classification and structured outputs; we can fine-tune on your sample prompts.
- open-llama-13b-quant (backup): lower cost for bulk batch scoring; acceptable if you favor throughput.

Resources I uploaded:
- Prompt set & small sample dataset: retailco_sample_prompts.txt (attached)
- Benchmark runner + previous evals: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c

Ask: please share 200–500 representative prompts (mix of edge cases) and any recent failure examples so our evals team can reproduce. Once we have that, Connor will run a side-by-side benchmark and produce a short regression diff report.

Next steps proposed:
1) You share sample prompts (you mentioned you could this week).
2) Redwood runs model fit evals and shares benchmark CSV + regression diff.
3) Quick call to review results and scope pin/rollback strategy if needed.

I can coordinate calendar for Wed/Thu next week — what works for you?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: retailco_sample_prompts.txt (text)

From: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@retailco.com>

Subject: Re: RetailCo discovery — model fit & next steps

Thanks Marissa — attaching the 250 prompts (mix of edge cases) you asked for. Also adding a quick note: after our internal model vendor pushed an upgrade last week (v1.2 -> v1.3), we started seeing a regression where the model is over-normalizing brand names in descriptions (examples in the attachment).

Quick context:
- Attached: retailco_sample_prompts.txt (250 prompts)
- Observed regression: previously acceptable outputs now drop brand tokens or conflate SKUs. Drives false positives in downstream dedup pipeline.
- Severity: ~3% of sampled items; impacts manual review workload.

Happy to run a short call — Wed 2/25 10am PT works for me. If you need additional logs I can pull examples from the last 48h.

—Sarah
VP Product, RetailCo
Sarah.Jones@retailco.com

Attachments: retailco_sample_prompts.txt (text)

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@retailco.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 07:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RetailCo discovery — model fit & regression concern

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for sending the prompts and the failure notes. Connor and I ran an initial side-by-side on a 500-sample subset and generated a short diff. Key findings:

- Benchmark summary (top-line): redwood-rlm-1.1 improves precision by ~9% on the prompt set vs. RetailCo's current provider v1.3 while keeping median latency ~320ms when warm. See attached benchmark_results_v1.2_vs_v1.3.csv for full metrics.
- Regression detail: the vendor v1.3 change appears to include an aggressive entity normalization pass that collapses brand tokens when context is ambiguous. We've reproduced the failure cases in our eval harness and captured text diffs (see regression_diff_report.pdf attached).

Operational mitigations we recommend:
1) Pinning strategy: pin RetailCo production route to model version v1.2 (vendor side) while we run a canary evaluation of redwood-rlm-1.1 on 5% of traffic for 2 business days. Pinning will avoid the immediate regression and give time for controlled comparison.
2) Canary rollout: 5% traffic -> 20% -> 100% if QA passes, with automatic rollback on detected precision drop >2.5%. We can configure this in Redwood Console and expose per-route metrics to your team.
3) Quick rollback option: if you prefer vendor rollback, we can help coordinate but recommend pinning on our side for faster stabilization.

Connor: can you add the small reproducible prompt set to the eval suite and produce an artifacts link (diff + sample traces)?

Sarah — Marissa will send an invite for Wed 2/25 10am PT. On the call we can review the diff PDF and choose pin vs. vendor-rollback.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: regression_diff_report.pdf, benchmark_results_v1.2_vs_v1.3.csv
